title: Yara and the Mixtape
premise: Jude Vane has spent seventeen years being the invisible gay kid in Halloway, a farming town of nine hundred, surviving on countdown calendars and mixtapes he makes for a boy he'll never name. When his grandmother dies and leaves him her recipe box, Jude finds index cards that aren't recipes at all — they're instructions for a small-town magic that lets him replay memories, including ones that reveal Halloway's championship-winning football dynasty was built on a bargain someone in his family made generations ago. As the season's last game approaches, Jude must choose between using the magic to erase himself from town memory forever or playing the game openly, with Eli Kessler at his side, knowing the truth will cost them both something they can't get back. He plays, tells the truth, and loses the trophy but wins the only championship that matters: a life where he is seen.
about_author: Dominic Iversen grew up in a prairie town smaller than the one he writes about, where Friday night lights were the closest thing to religion. He now lives in a city with better record stores and writes stories about kids who make their own light.

chapters.title: Ninety-Three Days
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the first day of senior year, Jude counts down to graduation, catalogs every person in Halloway who doesn't see him, and slips an unnamed mixtape into Eli Kessler's locker — a ritual three years running. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Grandma Ruthie dies suddenly; at the funeral no one cries except Jude. Sorting her kitchen, he finds the recipe box and notices card after card that reads like directions for something else entirely — 'stir until the room remembers you.' Emotional beat: grief cracking open curiosity.

chapters.title: Card Number One
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following a card's strange instructions in Ruthie's kitchen, Jude smells woodsmoke and hears his grandmother's voice at sixteen, laughing with a girl named Odette. The memory plays like a film only he can see. Emotional beat: wonder tangled with fear.

chapters.title: Two-Minute Drills
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli, Halloway's quarterback and Jude's secret best friend since childhood, feels the season's weight and the weight of the anonymous mixtapes he's kept in a shoebox. At practice he watches Jude in the stands and almost waves. Emotional beat: longing disguised as focus.

chapters.title: Odette Vane
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using more cards, Jude learns Odette was Ruthie's first love, driven out of Halloway in 1968 by a town that chose its football legacy over its conscience. The cards warn: 'the town keeps what it wins.' Emotional beat: righteous anger at inherited silence.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Almost
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Homecoming week; Eli's girlfriend Dana breaks up with him, sensing he's somewhere else. He finds Jude repainting the water tower sign as a prank and they laugh until it hurts, standing too close. Emotional beat: the almost-moment neither survives intact.

chapters.title: The Bargain Card
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Deep in the box, a card in different handwriting — his great-grandfather's — describes the bargain: Halloway trades one memory of shame per victory, and the town's glory is literally built on forgetting. Jude realizes his own erasure was part of the price. Emotional beat: horror of complicity.

chapters.title: Friday Night Lights Out
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Halloway wins its homecoming game; during the celebration, Jude tests a card and briefly becomes unnoticeable to everyone — even Eli walks past him. Emotional beat: invisibility revealed not as safety but as annihilation.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli finally confronts Jude about the mixtapes, having decoded that every track list spells out what Jude can't say. In Ruthie's kitchen, Jude admits everything — the cards, the magic, the years. Their first kiss tastes like terror and relief. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: What the Town Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Word spreads anyway — a photo, a rumor. Coach benchings, slashed tires, a note on the Vane door. Jude discovers the bargain feeds on exposed secrets: the more visible he becomes, the harder the town pushes back. Emotional beat: love under siege.

chapters.title: The Last Card
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The final card offers an out: perform the reversal during the championship, and Halloway forgets Jude Vane ever existed — safe, invisible, free. It's signed by Ruthie, written the week she died, addressed 'For my boy, if staying costs too much.' Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli finds the last card before Jude does and hides it, then confesses he did — arguing that forgetting isn't safety, it's surrender. They fight brutally in the empty stadium, saying the unforgivable. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth tearing in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Odette Returns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A letter arrives from Odette, now eighty, alive in Minneapolis, responding to Jude's research. She warns him: the bargain can be broken, but only by a Vane choosing to be remembered on purpose, in public, at cost. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as invitation.

chapters.title: Playoffs
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Halloway storms through the playoffs while the town splits — some students wear rainbow pins in solidarity, others vandalize Jude's truck. Eli plays angry and brilliant, dedicating each win silently to Jude. Emotional beat: defiance becoming momentum.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Kitchen, Again
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude replays Ruthie's final memory and learns she stayed in Halloway her whole life protecting the box, waiting for someone brave enough to break the bargain rather than hide inside it. Her last words: 'Don't do what I did, baby.' Emotional beat: blessing across generations.

chapters.title: The Apology
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Jude and Eli reconcile in the snow-covered stadium, trading honest apologies — Eli for hiding the card, Jude for asking Eli to be his secret. They decide together: play the final, tell the truth, keep the memory. Emotional beat: partnership over protection.

chapters.title: Championship Eve
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The night before the final, Jude burns every card except the bargain-breaker, writes his own card in Ruthie's style — 'serve warm, to the whole town' — and packs Odette's letter, his grandmother's photo, and a new mixtape labeled with both their names. Emotional beat: quiet resolve before the storm.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, rapid cuts. Championship day: Halloway versus their rivals, the stands packed, Odette arriving unannounced. Jude takes the field at halftime with a microphone instead of hiding, and begins telling nine hundred people exactly who he is. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage.

chapters.title: Breaking the Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. As Jude speaks, the magic resists — the crowd's faces blanking, the stadium flickering — and Eli runs onto the field to stand beside him, adding his voice. The bargain shatters like glass; decades of stolen memories flood back into the town at once. Emotional beat: collective reckoning.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Shaken but unbroken, Halloway returns to the game down by ten. Eli plays the fourth quarter of his life; Jude watches from the sideline holding Ruthie's box. Halloway loses by two points on a missed kick. Emotional beat: loss that feels strangely like victory.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the aftermath — some apologies, some slammed doors, Dana's hand on Jude's shoulder — the town must sit with everything it remembered. Odette and Jude visit Ruthie's grave together. The recipe box gets a new card: 'Yara' — Ruthie's secret name for hope. Emotional beat: mourning turned toward repair.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ninety-three days later, Jude crosses the stage holding Eli's hand in front of everyone, no countdown left to serve. He gives Eli a final mixtape — Side A titled 'Stay,' Side B blank, 'for everything we haven't lived yet.' Emotional beat: arrival, not escape.
